measures.questionText: To provide funding for City of Santee services and infrastructure, such as fixing streets and potholes; keeping streets, sidewalks, parks and public facilities safe, clean, and well-maintained; repairing/ replacing aging infrastructure and stormdrains; local traffic management; fire protection, paramedic, crime prevention, and 911 emergency response, shall City of Santee’s measure establishing a one cent sales tax be adopted, providing approximately $14,000,000 annually for city services for 10 years, with independent audits, citizens’ committee oversight, and all funds locally controlled?
measures.officialStatement:
CITY OF SANTEE
CITY ATTORNEY’S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE “Y”
1% GENERAL TRANSACTIONS AND USE (SALES) TAX
FOR TEN (10) YEARS

On June 24, 2026, the City Council voted to place Measure “Y” on the November 3,
2026 General Municipal Election ballot.

If approved by a majority of Santee voters, this Measure would authorize a one percent
(1%) retail transactions and use (sales) tax within the City of Santee. It is estimated that
Measure “Y” will provide an additional $14,000,000 in annual local funding for ten (10)
years that could be used for City of Santee services and infrastructure, including repairing
streets and potholes; cleaning and maintaining streets, sidewalks, parks and public
facilities, repairing and replacing stormdrains, local traffic management, fire protection,
paramedic, crime prevention, and 911 emergency response. This tax would be a “general
tax,” meaning that revenues raised from the tax would go into the City’s general fund to
pay for any lawful City program, improvement, or service.

The California Constitution (Proposition 218) and Revenue and Taxation Code section
7285.9 authorize the City to levy a general transactions and use/sales tax at a rate of one
percent (1%) so long as the tax is approved by a majority of the voters voting in an
election on that issue. If approved, the tax would become operative on April 1, 2027 and
remain in effect for ten (10) years until it expires on March 31, 2037. Any extension of
this tax beyond that date would require majority voter approval at a future City election.

Measure “Y” establishes a five (5) member Citizens’ Oversight Committee consisting of
Santee residents, property owners and business owners appointed by the City Council.
The Committee shall hold meetings open to the public pursuant to the California Brown
Act. Each year, City staff shall present a proposed annual spending plan to the
Committee, identifying City improvements, projects, programs, services proposed to be
funded with Measure “Y” revenues. The Committee may make recommendations about
the spending plan, which shall be incorporated into the City Manager’s proposed annual
budget and subject to City Council approval.

The Committee shall also be authorized to independently review the City’s annual
financial audit identifying Measure “Y” revenues collected and the expenditures made
from such revenues in the prior year. The Committee shall report their findings publicly,
including any concerns over use of Measure “Y” revenues, through an annual report
presented to the City Council at a public meeting.

The tax would be paid in addition to current sales taxes and would be collected at the
same time and in the same manner as existing sales taxes. All revenues raised by the tax
would remain in the City and would not be shared with the State, County or any other
agency.

A “yes” vote on Measure “Y” will authorize the 1% transactions and use (sales) tax for
10 years.

A “no” vote on Measure “Y” will not authorize the 1% transactions and use (sales) tax
for 10 years. “

 
The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure “Y”. If you desire a copy
of the Measure, please call the City Clerk’s Office at (619) 258-4100 or email at
clerk @cityofsanteeca.gov and a copy will be sent at no cost to you.

/s/ SHAWN HAGERTY
City Attorney

provenance.quote: To provide funding for City of Santee services and infrastructure, such as fixing streets and potholes; keeping streets, sidewalks, parks and public facilities safe, clean, and well-maintained; repairing/ replacing aging infrastructure and stormdrains; local traffic management; fire protection, paramedic, crime prevention, and 911 emergency response, shall City of Santee’s measure establishing a one cent sales tax be adopted, providing approximately $14,000,000 annually for city services for 10 years, with independent audits, citizens’ committee oversight, and all funds locally controlled?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add a 1% Santee sales and use tax, or $1 per $100 of taxable purchases, from April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2037. It would be added to existing sales taxes. The city estimates $14 million annually for its general fund, available for any lawful city program, improvement or service, including streets, parks, storm drains, public safety and emergency response. Existing legal tax exemptions remain. Revenue stays local. Annual independent financial audits and a five-member citizen oversight committee are required. Extending the tax beyond ten years would require majority voter approval at a future election. This measure also requires a majority vote.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional 1% tax for ten years and its spending-review and public-reporting rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not add this proposed ten-year 1% tax.

parts.label: Annual spending and citizen review
parts.what: The council appoints a five-member committee of city residents, property owners and business owners. Its meetings are public. It reviews the proposed annual spending plan before council budget approval, the annual financial audit, spending consistency and the council’s maintenance of effort compared with the three years before the ordinance. It presents an annual public report. If it reports a concern over tax revenue use, the council must place the matter on a public meeting agenda and respond on the record within 60 days. The committee recommends and reviews; the council approves the annual budget.
